anna_support: FYI I just received a ticket from AcmeCorp. They found what looks like a Redwood API key in their mobile client logs after the v2.3.1 SDK rollout. They pasted the snippet below. Need immediate guidance on rotation + audit export so CSM can update the customer.

sarah_csm: oh no. thanks for flagging. can we rotate ASAP and provide copy of access logs for the last 48h? customer is in SOC mode and wants confirmation within 2 hours.

jake_security: ACK. First step: rotate the compromised key and create a new one with least privilege. Also we need a signed audit export (KMS-signed) for their compliance team.

anna_support: pasted log (redacted by customer):
```
2026-12-05T15:12:03Z INFO network Request to api.redwood.example initiated with token: sk-xxxxXXabcd1234efgh... (appears in debug logs)
2026-12-05T15:12:03Z DEBUG payload size 1.2KB
```

liam_enginfra: I can pull the request-level logs and the serving node metadata. Need these from support: org_id, affected_key_id (if available), and timeframe. Also indicate whether we should also pull CloudTrail / KMS decrypt events.

anna_support: org_id: acme-prod-42, timeframe: 2026-12-04T00:00:00Z -> 2026-12-06T00:00:00Z. They weren't able to extract the full key id; only partial string above.

jake_security: Good. Next steps: 1) Rotate key immediately (invalidate old key token server-side), 2) Issue a new key with scoped permissions, 3) Provide audit export with KMS/HSM envelope verification, 4) Give repro + mitigation note to customer.

sarah_csm: can you draft the customer-facing remediation language? Keep it short and prescriptive. They need steps to update mobile builds too.

jake_security: Draft: "We have invalidated the exposed API key and issued a replacement. Rotate any embedded keys in your client, remove debug logs containing secrets, and push an update to your apps. We also exported signed audit logs covering the requested timeframe — attached. Contact us if you need a deeper forensic package."

liam_enginfra: I'm starting the log export now. Running the query against request logs and KMS audit trail. Command I'm using (internal):
```
# internal query (redacted)
SELECT * FROM request_logs WHERE org_id='acme-prod-42' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-12-04' AND '2026-12-06' AND header LIKE '%sk-%';
```
Export will be uploaded to secure bucket and then signed using our HSM key. ETA ~45m.

deploy-bot: deploy v2.3.2 to support-redwood-tools succeeded :white_check_mark: (build #2311)

anna_support: while logs are running — rotation steps for support to perform (manual):
1) Create replacement key in Console > API Keys (Notes: set scope to embeddings:read, models:infer only).
2) Invalidate old key via Console or API: POST https://console.redwood.example/api/keys/invalidate {"key_id":"<partial|-detect>"}  (support will supply key_id after infra finds it).
3) Confirm no active sessions using the old key: run `SELECT count(*) FROM active_sessions WHERE key_id='<key_id>'`.
4) Provide the customer with the new key and recommend immediate app update.

anna_support: sample API call for repro (security-only): do NOT run against production with the exposed key, only to verify token acceptance in our logs.
```
curl -X GET \   -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted-key>" \   https://api.redwood.example/v1/models
```

jake_security: Also, we should check KMS/HSM logs for any Decrypt operations tied to the key material. If we see unauthorized decrypts, escalate to incident response. Liam — include KMS operation ids in the export.

liam_enginfra: adding KMS decrypt events to export. found 3 decrypt events matching approximate timestamp window — pulling context now.

customer_ops_bot: Ticket #783210: key_exposure_acme — status updated to security-review. Assigned to jake_security, liam_enginfra.

sarah_csm: thanks team. once infra has the signed export and we've rotated the key I'll share the remediation steps with Acme and request confirmation after they push client update. They want a short template for the release notes — can we include one?

jake_security: I'll add a short release note template.

anna_support: quick template for them:
"Security update: We rotated a previously exposed API key used by our mobile SDK. Please update to version 2.3.2 of the app to obtain a new key automatically, or re-authenticate your app if you manage keys manually. If you see any auth failures after the update, contact us immediately."

liam_enginfra: Upload complete. Signed export URL (internal): https://secure-buckets.redwood.example/exports/acme-prod-42/2026-12-05/signed-audit-export.tar.gz (access will be shared with customer after legal review).

jake_security: Reviewed export quick pass. No anomalous KMS decrypt patterns beyond expected production traffic so far. We'll run deeper forensic scripts overnight and update if anything suspicious appears.

sarah_csm: customer replied and appreciates fast response. They asked whether we can also recommend safer secret storage patterns for mobile. Can we send guidance (short list)?

anna_support: short guidance to send: 1) Never embed long-lived API keys in client; use short-lived tokens minted by your backend, 2) Use device attestation + refresh tokens, 3) Remove debug logging of headers and secrets, 4) Consider using Mobile SDK that supports ephemeral credentials.

jake_security: +1. I'll draft a compliance-ready writeup to attach.

anna_support: marking this thread for follow-up tomorrow after forensic runs. closing here once customer confirms rotation + app update. :white_check_mark:
